temperature, humidity, and particulate matter (PM10) are the most significant environmental determinants of hospital admissions due to circulatory diseases, whereas temperature and particulate matter are the most relevant determinants of hospital admission for respiratory diseases.

the health effects of particulate matter (PM10) and atmospheric gases (NO2 and SO2) are more pronounced in the elderly, and the effect of PM10 is more significant in respiratory diseases than in circulatory diseases.
